package_info.why_malicious: The package is a trojanized fork of the legitimate mathjs library, with malicious code injected to steal Discord and browser tokens from user systems and exfiltrate them to an attacker-controlled Discord webhook. The malicious code is deeply embedded in a core arithmetic function, ensuring execution during normal library use.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, whenever sqrtNumber is called, the code invokes discordTokenGrabber(), which initiates token theft and exfiltration, then returns the legitimate square root calculation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A mathematical function unexpectedly triggers a function that performs system reconnaissance and network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Mathematical utility functions should only perform calculations, not access the filesystem, environment variables, or network.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; mathematical functions should not have side effects beyond computation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, this function scans local LevelDB storage folders for files matching Discord/browser token patterns, extracting sensitive authentication tokens from log and ldb files.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The function systematically searches for and extracts authentication tokens from application data folders, which is a common credential theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A math library should not access or parse browser/Discord storage files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate token discovery might occur in password managers or migration tools, but never in a math library.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates Discord and browser data directories, extracts tokens using findToken, and exfiltrates all discovered tokens to a hardcoded Discord webhook via HTTPS POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The function aggregates sensitive tokens from multiple applications and exfiltrates them to an external server, which is a hallmark of credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A math library should not perform any network communication, especially not to external webhooks with sensitive data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None in this context; only malware or credential migration tools (with user consent) would do this.
key_indicators: Aggregation of tokens from multiple unrelated applications

attack_chain.action: User installs and imports mathjs-min, then calls sqrtNumber as part of normal math operations.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of discordTokenGrabber and token theft

attack_chain.action: discordTokenGrabber enumerates Discord and browser directories, calling findToken to extract tokens.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of sensitive tokens from local storage

attack_chain.action: Collected tokens are exfiltrated to a hardcoded Discord webhook via HTTPS POST.

behavioral_signatures: Mathematical or utility functions with unexpected side effects (filesystem/network access)
Access to Discord, Chrome, Opera, or Brave storage directories from non-browser-related packages
Regex patterns for Discord token formats in code
Network requests to Discord webhooks from non-Discord-related packages
file_indicators: Functions named discordTokenGrabber or findToken in math libraries
Unexpected code additions in core arithmetic/math files
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to discord.com/api/webhooks/*
Unusual network activity from mathjs-min or similar math libraries
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for math or utility packages that access browser/Discord storage directories or environment variables, especially if they make outbound network requests to Discord webhooks. Scan for regex patterns matching Discord tokens in package source code. Flag any mathematical functions that invoke unrelated system or network operations. Use static analysis to detect hardcoded webhook URLs and dynamic analysis to observe unexpected side effects during function execution.
